sections.overview: Pseudargyrotoza conwagana is a small tortrix moth found across much of Europe and parts of Asia.
sections.identification: A conspicuous yellow patch on the resting adult’s forewings helps identify it; its wingspan is about eleven to fifteen millimetres.
sections.habitat: In Britain it is recorded in places where ash and privet grow.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed chiefly on ash and can also use privet; European records include larvae in the fruits or seeds of ash, privet and barberry.
sections.behavior: Adults are often seen flying by day near ash, and in Britain the main flight period runs from late spring into summer.
sections.reproduction: The sources reviewed describe host plants but not a complete life cycle.
sections.ecology: Larvae use several host plants, especially ash.
sections.conservation: No global conservation assessment was found in the sources consulted.
